detail.abstract:
Purpose of the study: This study aimed to determine the influence of the teachers' soft skills on science process capabilities and academic performance of grade 11 students in public high schools in clusters IV and V during the S.Y. 2021-2022. This study also sought to determine the significant difference between the science process capabilities and academic performance of male and female grade 11 students in Earth and Life Science. 

Methodology: Explanatory sequential research design was utilized. The respondents included 33 science teachers and 376 grade 11 students. Data were collected through validated surveys, observation checklists, academic records, and interviews. Analysis was conducted using statistical software for quantitative data and thematic review for qualitative responses. 

Main Findings: Teachers strongly utilized their soft skills. Students demonstrated effective science process capabilities. Academic performance in Science was outstanding. No significant difference in science process capabilities between male and female students. However, female students performed better academically in Earth and Life Science. Moreover, significant positive relationships were found between teachers' soft skills and students' science process capabilities and academic performance. 

Novelty/Originality of this study: This study highlights the impact of teachers' soft skills on both science process capabilities and academic performance in the new normal. Moreover, this study contributes to the limited empirical evidence linking teachers' soft skills with both science process capabilities and academic performance in the post-pandemic blended learning context, offering insights for enhancing teaching strategies and professional development in senior high school science education.

title: Ambiguity Aversion and the Limits of Strategic Vagueness
affiliations: and

detail.title: Ambiguity Aversion and the Limits of Strategic Vagueness
detail.abstract: A large literature holds that deliberate vagueness in force majeure (FM) and material-adverse-change (MAC) clauses is efficient: vague standards screen opportunistic claims, preserve flexibility, and elicit information. That conclusion assumes parties price ambiguous contingencies at expected value. We relax the assumption: facing genuinely novel catastrophes, parties weight worst cases over a set of priors, as Ellsberg documented. In an alpha-maxmin bargaining model, each reservation price decomposes into an SEU value and an ambiguity premium, and the premia sum to an "ambiguity tax" that continuously contracts the certainty-equivalent surplus (Result 1). Price concessions are the tax's incidence and require asymmetric premia (Corollary 1); the tax increases in aversion, prior-set width, and exposures (Result 2); and vagueness improves on precise drafting only while its screening and information benefits exceed the tax, a conditional inversion of the strategic-vagueness results (Result 3). Non-closure is the limiting tail. The framework organizes the COVID-19 force majeure docket and the Delaware material-adverse-effect canon, and yields three reforms, each keyed to one parameter of the tax: objectively indexed triggers, mandatory renegotiation, and an ambiguity-aware interpretive canon.

title: Algorithms, Biases, and Belief Polarization
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - NUS Business School, University of Michigan Ross School of Business and The Stephen M. Ross School of Business at the University of Michigan

detail.title: Algorithms, Biases, and Belief Polarization
detail.abstract: Algorithmic curation by social media platforms is often blamed for rising polarization. Yet intrinsic biases in how humans process information, such as signal distortion (perceiving information as more aligned with one's belief) and weight distortion (discounting belief-incongruent information), can also contribute. This paper investigates the relative contributions of these two pathways and examines how the engagement metric the algorithm optimizes, such as dwell time or likes, shapes outcomes. Our four-step approach combines (1) an online experiment tracking belief updating and engagement, (2) model estimation, (3) deep reinforcement learning agents trained on the estimated model to emulate personalized recommenders, and (4) counterfactual simulations of posterior belief distributions. We find that information-processing biases and algorithmic curation each amplify polarization to a similar degree. Among biases, weight distortion is the primary channel. Because individuals dislike opposing content yet spend more time reading it than confirmatory content, like-maximizing and dwelltime-maximizing algorithms curate divergent feeds. Both increase polarization relative to random assignment, but dwell-time maximization leads to less polarized beliefs than like maximization.

title: The Little Dress and the Big Fall: Thomas Mann's "Luischen," the Humiliated Male, and the Cultural Logic of Sissification - The Whip and the Ledger: Thomas Mann’s Luischen, the Pathology of the “Little Man,” and the Modern BDSM Narrative as Re-Scripted Cruelty

detail.title: The Little Dress and the Big Fall: Thomas Mann's "Luischen," the Humiliated Male, and the Cultural Logic of Sissification - The Whip and the Ledger: Thomas Mann’s Luischen, the Pathology of the “Little Man,” and the Modern BDSM Narrative as Re-Scripted Cruelty
detail.abstract: Thomas Mann's 1897 satirical novella Luischen (often translated as Little Lizzy) has long been read as a grotesque morality tale of bourgeois marriage. This essay radically recontextualizes the story, arguing that it operates as a prophetic cultural text prefiguring the late twentieth-and twenty-first-century psychosexual dynamics of forced feminization, sissy humiliation, and the rise of the dominatrix without structural power. Drawing on classical psychoanalysis (Freud, Lacan), left psychoanalysis (Žižek), poststructuralist gender theory (Butler, Foucault), and contemporary cultural criticism of BDSM, trans, and sissy subcultures, the analysis traces how Christian Jacoby's coerced performance as a chansonette singer stages the foundational scene of male symbolic castration through cross-dressing.

title: Do Retirement Benefits Shape Auditor Turnover and Audit Quality? Evidence from Big 4 Auditors
affiliations: The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Clemson University and University of Connecticut - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Do Retirement Benefits Shape Auditor Turnover and Audit Quality? Evidence from Big 4 Auditors
detail.abstract: Audit firms rely heavily on human capital, yet little is known about how retirement benefits affect auditor turnover and audit quality. We examine whether the generosity of Big 4 audit firms’ retirement benefits—focusing on defined contribution (DC) plans, the dominant form of retirement benefits in the accounting profession—affects auditor turnover and audit quality. Using novel data from Form 5500 filings, we find that higher DC plan generosity is associated with lower auditor turnover and higher audit quality. A path analysis suggests that the improvement in audit quality occurs primarily through a reduction in auditor turnover, consistent with human capital retention as the underlying mechanism. To strengthen causal inference, we conduct two difference-in-differences analyses using KPMG (PwC)'s 2022 (2008) firm-wide increase (decrease) in the generosity of its DC benefits and find that KPMG (PwC)’s audit quality increased (decreased) more than that of other Big 4 firms following the policy adjustment. Cross-sectional analyses demonstrate that the impact of DC plan generosity on audit quality is more pronounced for larger and more complex clients, where auditor continuity is likely most valuable. Results are robust to controlling for salary. Overall, our findings contribute to the literature on auditor compensation, audit labor markets, and audit quality, and highlight how retirement benefit design can influence audit outcomes, which is important to audit firms, audit clients, investors, and regulators amid complex and dynamic audit labor markets.

title: AI Summaries and Online Review Contributions: Effects on Modality Choice and Content Novelty
affiliations: , , University of Science and Technology of China (USTC),  and University of Wisconsin-Madison - Wisconsin School of Business

detail.title: AI Summaries and Online Review Contributions: Effects on Modality Choice and Content Novelty
detail.abstract: Online platforms increasingly use generative AI to summarize user-generated content and facilitate consumer decision making, yet little is known about how different forms of summaries shape users' content contribution behavior. We examine the effects of two types of AI summaries on review contributions: textbased AI summaries (TAIS), which summarize textual content only, and multimodal AI summaries (MAIS), which jointly summarize review text and images. Drawing on social comparison theory, we conceptualize AI summaries as salient comparison benchmarks that motivate contributors to differentiate their reviews from AI-generated representations of existing content and avoid redundant contributions. We propose a dual-path differentiation framework, in which contributors, motivated by a need for uniqueness, respond by (i) shifting contributions toward the modality not emphasized by AI summaries (modality differentiation) and (ii) increasing the semantic novelty of content within the modality emphasized by AI summaries (semantic differentiation). Leveraging quasi-natural experiments surrounding the introduction of TAIS and MAIS on two leading online travel agency platforms in China, we find support for this dual-path differentiation framework. Specifically, TAIS increases the proportion of multimodal reviews (i.e., reviews that combine text and images) while increasing the semantic novelty of text-only reviews. In contrast, MAIS decreases the proportion of multimodal reviews, shifting contributions toward text-only reviews, while increasing the semantic novelty of images within multimodal reviews. Together, these findings demonstrate how AI summaries affect reviewer behavior by shaping how reviewers allocate effort across modalities and differentiate from existing content. Our findings offer new principles for digital platforms to understand and manage user-generated content in the presence of AI summaries.

title: Digitalization as an Enabler of ESG Transparency Value Relevance: Evidence from European Firms
affiliations: FOM University of Applied Sciences - ESSEN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Digitalization as an Enabler of ESG Transparency Value Relevance: Evidence from European Firms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This study examines how ESG transparency affects the firm value of European publicly listed companies, highlighting the moderating role of digitalization. Using panel data from STOXX Europe 600 firms (2020-2023; 1,763 firm-year observations), we employ the Bloomberg ESG Disclosure Score, Tobin's Q and a validated text-mining-based digitalization index based on 524 technologyrelated terms across four technology clusters. Panel regressions show that ESG transparency alone does not significantly affect firm value. Overall digitalization, especially AI and automation, appear to act as conditional moderators that shape the relationship between ESG transparency and firm value. Interaction-and robustness analyses partially confirm the relevance of overall digitalization and AI/automation effects. The findings suggest that strategic integration of ESG and digital initiatives, particularly AI and automation, can potentially enhance firm value, though observed effects remain econometrically limited. Other digital technologies, while conceptually supportive by providing data and capacity, exhibit no significant direct effects on firm value. The analysis contributes to the literature by addressing methodological nuances, including interaction effect interpretation, measurement issues and endogeneity concerns and discusses approaches in prior ESG/digitalization research. Additionally, practical implications for corporate strategy and regulatory compliance (e.g. CSRD) are provided. Future research could evaluate advanced machine learning and NLP approaches to better capture AI's role in ESG reporting, taking into account the perspectives regarding both the potential and current limitations of commonly used digitalization proxies highlighted in this study.

title: Optimizing E-commerce Same-Day Fulfillment: Truck-Drone Routing with Forward Warehouses and Order Splitting
affiliations: Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University and University of Bristol

detail.title: Optimizing E-commerce Same-Day Fulfillment: Truck-Drone Routing with Forward Warehouses and Order Splitting
detail.abstract: With the development of same-day e-commerce services, forward warehouses (FWs) and drone delivery have been widely adopted to improve urban last-mile fulfillment efficiency. However, limited FW inventories continue to restrict fulfillment efficiency. Meanwhile, the growth of reverse logistics demand makes trucks a mandatory service resource within the system. To address this issue, this study considers a three-echelon network comprising FWs, a central depot, and customers, and incorporates an order-splitting delivery strategy to enhance customer fulfillment efficiency and inventory utilization. We develop a mixed-integer linear programming model for the truck-drone pickup and delivery problem with order splitting. By explicitly considering inventory status, order product categories, and fleet resources, we jointly optimize customer assignment, resource allocation, and routing decisions. Under the framework of large neighborhood search, we develop a customized Inventory-Aware Marginal Bidding heuristic and introduce a large language model-enhanced operator pool to enrich the neighborhood search structure. Numerical experiments validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm and reveal several managerial insights. Specifically, the order-splitting strategy effectively overcomes fulfillment bottlenecks caused by limited inventory; moderately increasing inventory buffers and drone payload capacity helps improve the drone fulfillment ratio; and higher pickup demand strengthens truck route rigidity and weakens drone service flexibility. This study provides decision support for coordinating FW inventory utilization, truck resource allocation, and drone-enabled rapid fulfillment in same-day e-commerce operations.

title: Hidden Costs, Biased Decisions: Predicting and Optimizing E-Retailer Shipping Charges Under Information Asymmetry
affiliations: ,  and Texas A&M University - Department of Information & Operations Management

detail.title: Hidden Costs, Biased Decisions: Predicting and Optimizing E-Retailer Shipping Charges Under Information Asymmetry
detail.abstract: When e-retailers outsource order fulfillment, the packing and shipping decisions made by third-party logistics (3PL) providers are largely opaque, making actual shipping charges difficult to predict at the point of sale. Within the 3PL itself, a further information asymmetry arises: base charges are calculable from published common carrier rate tables, but accessorial charges, surcharges assessed after delivery, remain hidden until the carrier invoices the fulfillment 3PL, and the 3PL passes it on to the e-retailer. This paper investigates how this partial observability distorts operational decisions and how machine learning (ML) can mitigate the resulting inefficiency. We develop sequential learning ML models that capture the cascading structure of 3PL fulfillment decisions (packing → carrier selection → charges), outperforming standard ML benchmarks for both base and accessorial charge prediction. We then integrate these predictions into a predict-then-optimize approach for shipping method selection, yielding meaningful expected cost savings relative to actual 3PL decisions. Finally, leveraging a regression discontinuity analysis at the base-charge indifference boundary, we provide causal evidence that the hidden accessorial charge component systematically distorts carrier selection. These three stages-prediction, optimization, and causation-form a methodological framework for diagnosing and correcting decision bias under partial observability.

title: Pricing AI Services with Data-Use Rights
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen), University of Michigan at Ann Arbor and California State University Fullerton

detail.title: Pricing AI Services with Data-Use Rights
detail.abstract: AI service platforms sell current access while deciding which customer interactions may be used for future model improvement. This creates a tension absent from standard service menus: the usage price that protects premium restricted-use plans from cannibalization may be too high to procure valuable training usage, while the price that buys data may undermine premium separation. We study nonlinear service menus in which each contract specifies an access fee, a usage price, and a data-use right. Against blanket data policies that either train on all served usage or restrict all served usage, we characterize when targeted data procurement is optimal. A low-tier data-sharing plan can buy useful interactions and, when premium users have higher training-use burdens, make the cheap plan less attractive to them. The relevant value of data is menu-adjusted: continuation-value gains net of user burdens, information rents, and any repair needed to preserve self-selection. Numerical analyses illustrate that targeted procurement can outperform train-all policies even while collecting less raw data. The analysis yields a select-price-repair-retire rule: select tiers whose data value survives these costs, price data sharing as procurement rather than a generic subsidy, repair menus that create positive self-selection cycles, and retire discounts once marginal continuation value falls below the rent burden.

title:
When Founder Wealth Becomes Capital: Organizational Form and Top-Wealth Persistence 
Evidence from Founder Deaths
affiliations: , Macau University of Science and Technology, Macau University of Science and Technology and Macau University of Science and Technology

detail.title:
When Founder Wealth Becomes Capital: Organizational Form and Top-Wealth Persistence 
Evidence from Founder Deaths
detail.abstract: Founder-made business fortunes often begin as claims on owner-specific human capital rather than portable capital. We study organizational conversion: when such wealth becomes transferable family capital. We build a hand-audited global panel linking 47,626 billionaire person-years, 36,898 family-fortune-years, and 313 founder deaths to BoardEx, Capital IQ, Orbis ownership histories, public filings, source firms, holding vehicles, and RAND HRS external validation. Founder death lowers family-fortune survival by about 59 percentage points. Among death events, pre-existing organizational architecture predicts 29.3 and 33.8 percentage-point higher survival at three and five years and shifts the 50 percent three-year survival threshold from $14.8 billion to $4.7 billion. Source-firm operating performance does not explain the premium. In a narrower Orbis branch, high-architecture cases are more likely to have low pre-death exposure to the original source firm. A continuation model implies that removing architecture lowers high-architecture survival by 6.8, 12.9, and 16.1 points over one, three, and five years. Organizational form is a wealth-preservation technology: it separates the family wealth claim from personalized founder exposure.

title: GenAI-Powered Safety and Permit-to-Work Automation Integrated with SAP Enterprise Asset Management

detail.title: GenAI-Powered Safety and Permit-to-Work Automation Integrated with SAP Enterprise Asset Management
detail.abstract: Permit-to-work systems are critical administrative controls for hazardous maintenance and field execution activities in asset-intensive industries. Many permit processes remain dependent on manual review, fragmented asset context, and inconsistent retrieval of safety procedures. Enterprise asset management systems, including SAP EAM, contain structured information about technical objects, functional locations, maintenance orders, task lists, historical failures, and work execution status. This review examines how generative artificial intelligence and retrieval-augmented generation can support safety and permit-to-work automation when grounded in enterprise asset data and controlled safety knowledge. The paper synthesizes literature on large language models for safety assessment, electronic permit-to-work systems, occupational safety analytics, predictive maintenance, and Industry 4.0 asset management. The review finds that GenAI can assist with hazard identification, procedure retrieval, permit drafting, risk-control recommendation, and lessons-learned summarization. However, current research also shows important limitations involving reliability, explainability, validation, accountability, and measurable safety outcomes. The paper proposes a human-in-the-loop SAFE-EAM framework that connects SAP EAM data, approved safety procedures, isolation controls, predictive maintenance signals, and auditable GenAI outputs. The contribution is a practical taxonomy, comparison matrix, research gap matrix, maturity model, and implementation roadmap for high-hazard industries such as oil and gas, utilities, chemicals, mining, and heavy manufacturing.

title: Reducing Food Waste Through Profit-Driven Digital Applications
affiliations: University of West Attica

detail.title: Reducing Food Waste Through Profit-Driven Digital Applications
detail.abstract: This paper examines the contribution of new technologies in reducing food waste through real, profit-driven applications in the retail and food service sectors. Based on data from the UN and Eurostat, the environmental and economic footprint of the problem in Greece and the EU is analyzed. Through the description of the Too Good To Go platform, it is highlighted how digital tools provide economic incentives to businesses for managing surplus food. In conclusion, it is proven that technological innovation can successfully align business profitability with environmental sustainability.

title: Measuring AI Aging in UPI Fraud Detection: A PSI-Based Drift Monitor Evaluated on a No-Drift Benchmark, with Synthetic Validation of an Adaptive Retraining Trigger
affiliations: Ravenshaw University and Ravenshaw University

detail.title: Measuring AI Aging in UPI Fraud Detection: A PSI-Based Drift Monitor Evaluated on a No-Drift Benchmark, with Synthetic Validation of an Adaptive Retraining Trigger
detail.abstract: India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processes over 13 billion monthly transactions, but fraud detection models suffer from “AI aging”, accuracy decays as transaction patterns shift. To date, no study has measured how quickly UPI fraud models degrade or built a retraining framework tailored to India’s regulatory and computational constraints. Using a public Kaggle dataset (300,113 training transactions, January–September 2023; 99,887 test transactions, October–December 2023), we trained five individual models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) and a stacking ensemble. A short-term temporal degradation experiment over three months showed static models lost roughly two recall percentage points per month. We monitored drift weekly using the Population Stability Index (PSI) on transaction amounts, along with JS divergence, Wasserstein distance, MMD, and a classifier-based two-sample test. An adaptive retraining trigger fires when PSI > 0.2; we compared this drift-triggered strategy against static, monthly, and quarterly retraining. The chronological test period exhibited no significant drift across all metrics. Consequently, the drift-triggered strategy never retrained, matching the static model’s final recall (94.2%) while saving 100% of retraining costs. Monthly retraining required 268 seconds and ended with lower recall (92.5%). The stacking ensemble achieved 92.9% recall; CatBoost, the best individual model, reached 93.9% recall, exceeding the literature benchmark of 90%. To evaluate the retraining component, three synthetic drift-injection experiments (sudden fraud-rate shift, gradual covariate shift, and concept drift) confirmed that the PSI trigger fires within 1–2 weeks of a change-point and that a single retraining cycle restores recall to within 1–2 points of the pre-drift baseline. Our code and data splits are publicly available.

title: The Paradox of AI Familiarity in Electronic Commerce: A Comparative Preference Analysis with Traditional Search Engines
affiliations: Chosun University

detail.title: The Paradox of AI Familiarity in Electronic Commerce: A Comparative Preference Analysis with Traditional Search Engines
detail.abstract: While conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally revolutionizing the information search market, consumers paradoxically continue to rely on traditional search engines for product purchasing decisions such as online shopping. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms of consumer adoption of conversational AI versus traditional search engines specifically within the product purchase search process. Across three sequential studies, this research aims to uncover how consumers evaluate and adopt conversational AI in comparison to traditional search engines. Study 1 establishes a baseline by revealing that consumers persistently prefer traditional search engines, yielding significantly higher trust and more favorable attitudes than AI. Furthermore, this research identifies a conditional mechanism where consumer trust is shaped by the interplay between the search environment and task characteristics. Specifically, Study 2 reveals that ad-filtering improves AI trust only for low-involvement products, while high-involvement contexts exhibit persistent algorithm aversion. Moreover, a choice-based conjoint (CBC) analysis uncovers unobserved consumer heterogeneity, identifying three distinct segments (Study 3). Notably, this research discovers a ‘paradoxical rejection’ phenomenon where the segment with the highest AI familiarity strictly avoids AI for shopping tasks. This active resistance is driven by heightened persuasion knowledge and the inherent risks of AI. These findings offer critical academic and practical implications for AI integration in electronic commerce, explicitly challenging the linear adoption assumptions of traditional technology acceptance models by demonstrating the decoupling of affective attitude and cognitive trust, and providing strategic guidelines for designing future shopping interfaces.

detail.abstract: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) is widely used in business, marketing, information-systems, and behavioral research, but the de-facto standard implementation, SmartPLS 4, is closed-source and commercially licensed. We introduce openpls-engine, an open-source Python library released under GPL-3.0 that implements PLS-SEM, its associated quality criteria (HTMT, SRMR, d_ULS, f² , Q² , Cronbach α, Dijkstra-Henseler ρ_A), and advanced analyses (multi-group analysis, Importance-Performance Map Analysis, two-stage moderation, FIMIX-PLS finite-mixture segmentation, PLSpredict, and two inner-weighting schemes beyond the classical centroid/factorial/path schemes). We validate the engine against SmartPLS 4 on 14 reference cases covering canonical PLS-SEM models (ECSI, ACSI, TAM, UTAUT, Organisational Identification and a variation thereof, Employee Retention, and the Corporate Reputation primer in its simple, extended, advanced, and four redundancy-analysis variants). All path coefficients, R² values, indicator loadings, outer weights, and HTMT ratios match the SmartPLS reference within an absolute tolerance of |∆| < 0.001 across all 14 cases for the path-weighting scheme, with one known divergence under FACTORIAL inner-weighting on n = 98 that we trace to an optimisation-basin selection rather than an algorithmic defect. A small, bounded SRMR offset (+0.002 to +0.011, well below the conventional 0.08 fit threshold) is fully characterised in Section 6. The library is published on PyPI (pip install openpls-engine) and the source repository is publicly available; all validation scripts and reference sidecars are released alongside the paper so that any reported value can be reproduced from a clean environment.

detail.abstract: Modern software systems operate in environments characterized by continuous change, high availability expectations, and complex failure modes. This paper proposes a comprehensive practitioner’s framework for resilient architecture, organized around four pillars: a mental model that distinguishes robustness, resilience, and antifragility; a set of antifragile organizational rituals (blameless post-mortems, controlled chaos experiments, and quarterly architecture reviews); a pragmatic governance approach that unifies financial and operational metrics; and a team-topology strategy that structures human capital for adaptability. The central thesis is that sustainable resilience is primarily a sociotechnical challenge: understanding business needs deeply and building the organizational habits and feedback loops required to respond to change is more decisive than any individual architectural pattern.

Why do the same difficulties recur - in relationships, at work, inside our own minds -even when everyone
is trying their best? This paper offers a single lens. Every system runs on two ingredients: C, the structure
everyone can see and knows everyone can see, and V, the noise and room for interpretation that keeps it
from freezing. Their ratio, S = C/V, appears to govern whether a system coordinates, stalls, or comes
apart. A memoryless two-agent simulation shows not a gradual improvement but a phase transition:

Dual Agency and Goal Incongruence in Influencer Platforms
detail.abstract: Social AI agents are increasingly deployed on social media platforms to stimulate user engagement. Although prior research highlights the engagement benefits, users may interpret AI involvement as a manipulative persuasion attempt when their interests and influencers' interests are not fully aligned. We conduct a randomized field experiment on a leading online video-sharing platform to understand how comments posted by social AI agents affect viewer engagement with influencers' videos. The experiment compares two content genres that differ in goal incongruence between influencers and viewers: (i) Cooking Tutorials videos, where influencers' instructional goals largely align with viewers' learning objectives, and (ii) Restaurant Discovery videos, where influencers' commercial incentives may conflict with viewers' desire for authentic, unbiased recommendations. Within each genre, influencers are randomly assigned to either a treatment condition in which AI comments are posted on newly released videos, or a control condition without AI comments. The results reveal asymmetric effects. In low-goal-incongruence settings (Cooking Tutorials), AI comments increase viewer engagement, including likes, shares, and comments. In contrast, in high-goal-incongruence settings (Restaurant Discovery), AI comments reduce engagement, and the negative effect is stronger for influencers with greater advertising content in their prior videos. A complementary online experiment further shows that in high-goal-incongruence settings, AI comments reduce engagement by increasing perceived manipulative intent. Our findings identify goal incongruence as a boundary condition for the effectiveness of AI-generated social interactions and underscore the importance of aligning AI engagement strategies with users' trust expectations.

detail.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping decision-making processes across a range of domains. While existing research has primarily focused on how AI improves efficiency, coordination, and optimization, less attention has been given to how AI participates in the formation of problems themselves. This paper examines how AI systems-and increasingly AI agents-contribute to problem formation in real-world contexts. Drawing on empirical illustrations from semiconductor manufacturing, engineering design, and logistics systems, it shows that AI is not only used to solve predefined problems, but also to define anomalies, expand design spaces, and reshape demand anticipation. Although the cases primarily involve AI systems rather than fully autonomous AI agents, they reveal an emerging pattern of cognitive participation, in which AI contributes to interpretation, hypothesis generation, and the construction of problem definitions. In this sense, current AI systems can be understood as early forms of agent-like behavior. The findings point to a broader transition from socio-technical systems toward socio-cognitive multi-agent systems, where problems are no longer treated as fixed inputs, but as dynamic outcomes of human-AI interaction.

detail.abstract:
As the development rate of AI began to gain momentum in this digital era, it has initiated a revolution in the field of marketing, which none could ever think of. The moment it was deemed possible to alleviate such tiresome operations and create real-time, personalized experiences, technologies related to AI began changing the existing trend by which brands interact with their consumers. In this regard, start-ups are expected to reap the benefits of such developments at a larger scale, unlike other more established and resource-intensive companies or groups of enterprises. They can leverage technologies related to AI, which, by being cost-effective, will help them formulate strategies that do not only reach the targeted consumers but also engage them on a deeper, more significant level. The capability to operate at larger scales without charging such costs provides start-ups with a stepping stone towards developing a competitive advantage compared to others. The marketing solutions offered by technologies related to AI, such as the automation of customer service through chatbots, recommendation engines, and predictive analytics, have already proved its worth with respect to enhancing customer experiences. Nevertheless, in spite of the speedy increase in their uptake, there remains a conceptual void about their long-run contribution to customer engagement and brand loyalty in the entrepreneurial and start-up environment. The majority of what has been written to date centers on either the technical competence of AI or the marketing performance results of AI in the short run; in other words, there has been no noticeable attention to the lion’s share of AI-applications--namely, their contribution to long-run consumer brand relationships. This current study undertakes the development of a conceptual model that integrates AI marketing applications with customer engagement and brand loyalty constructs in the digital start-up environment. The conceptual model is grounded in service-dominant logic and relationship marketing theories with value being seen as something that should be produced between firms and customers over time that should be appropriate for all individuals. It implies an improvement in different aspects of engaging activities such as interactive communication, offers, and services by marketing machinery fueled by AI. This, in turn, has given rise to the concept of a mediating influence on brand loyalty and AI adoption. There has also been consideration of the start-up context as a moderating factor in this model to incorporate the aspects of entrepreneurial flexibility and innovation culture.

It also allows for various situations through the direct and indirect routes of association. The direct route is used to address situations in which the application of AI tools will be subject to brand loyalty through enhanced perceptions of innovativeness and distinction of brand.

title: Metatorial: Articulating the Essential Practices of Open Access Publishing in an Age of AI Knowledge Systems

detail.title: Metatorial: Articulating the Essential Practices of Open Access Publishing in an Age of AI Knowledge Systems
detail.abstract:
Open Access (OA) publishing has expanded access to scholarly research through a growing ecosystem of collective funding models, institutional partnerships, and community-supported publishing initiatives. At the same time, the increasing complexity of OA funding environments, combined with the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-mediated knowledge systems, has exposed a largely overlooked challenge: understanding not only what scholarly content becomes openly available, but also how that content is selected, funded, organized, discovered, preserved, and sustained over time.

This paper introduces metatorial, a framework developed by Mirela Roncevic to describe and examine a set of essential yet often fragmented or overlooked practices within contemporary OA publishing. Positioned between editorial practice and institutional stewardship, metatorial focuses on the evaluative, organizational, communicative, and continuity-related activities meant to shape both the funding of OA content and its long-term visibility across scholarly and knowledge environments.

The paper introduces the concepts of metatorial imprint and metatorial footprint to distinguish between pre-funding and post-publication responsibilities within the OA ecosystem. It further proposes metatorial as an inventory process through which institutions, libraries, publishers, funders, intermediaries, and scholarly communities can examine seven interconnected dimensions of OA publishing: content, participation, representation, funding, discovery, visibility, and continuity.

Rather than offering a checklist or compliance framework, metatorial provides a way of understanding how collective publishing decisions shape the scholarly environments they help create. At a time when openly available research increasingly informs both scholarship and AI systems, the paper argues that greater attention to these interconnected dimensions and activities can strengthen the coherence, relevance, discoverability, and long-term value of the research being collectively funded and supported.

detail.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into digital health platforms has transformed the landscape of mental health support and stress management. Yet the predominant research focus remains on algorithmic performance rather than on how AI systems influence human behavior and decision-making. This study examines the intersection of behavior informatics and digital health, analyzing how AI-driven systems shape human decision behavior in mental health and stress management contexts. Using a mixed-methods framework grounded in behavioral theory, technology acceptance models, and AI ethics, the study explores cognitive and behavioral factors-including trust, perceived usefulness, emotional state, and user autonomy-that mediate interactions between individuals and AI-generated recommendations. Three hypotheses are proposed: (H1) AI-driven digital health systems significantly influence human decision-making; (H2) greater transparency and explainability in AI systems increase user trust; and (H3) higher trust in AI recommendations correlates with greater adherence to AI-guided behavioral suggestions. Key literature gaps are identified, including the absence of behavior-informed evaluation frameworks, insufficient study of post-adoption decision behavior, and underdeveloped empirically grounded ethical analysis. This paper argues for the systematic integration of behavioral informatics principles into the design, deployment, and governance of digital mental health technologies to ensure ethical, effective, and humancentered outcomes.

Narrative Entropy (S n) is a structural-complexity construct of the Bulut Doctrine that quantifies the cognitive resistance and causal uncertainty a narrative imposes on a reader across time. Because the construct has been developed incrementally across the corpus, its operational expression has appeared in more than one form. This note serves a single purpose: to fix, in one place, the canonical definition of S n , to document the version history of its operationalisation, and to state plainly the one open formal problem that remains unresolved. It makes no new empirical claim. It is a reference and disambiguation document, not a validation study. The canonical general form is the time integral of the product of Information Friction and Causal Branching; the product form S n = I f × C b × t used in the registered pilot is its scene-constant special case. The known dimensional inconsistency of the product form is documented here as an open question, consistent with the pilot report that first recorded it.

detail.abstract: We describe our search for a viable theory of the firm that bridges the gap between accounting practice and theory. First, we describe Michael Jensen's role in the development of the economic theory of the firm in accounting and his recognition of the need to develop a more viable theory later in life. Second, we describe the motivation of the co-authors to develop a pragmatic theory of the firm that captures long-term value creation using GAAP-based financial statements and incorporates shared values and social norms. Third, we demonstrate how applying practical accounting insights from the Pragmatic Theory of the Firm and the Balanced Scorecard increases the usefulness of the theory of the firm to accounting practitioners, researchers, and educators. We conclude by describing how our approach helps the accounting profession address 21st-century challenges including environmental and social issues, sustainability, and accounting for intangibles.

title: Token-Efficient Structured Data Representation for Financial Document Analysis: A TOON-Based Approach

detail.title: Token-Efficient Structured Data Representation for Financial Document Analysis: A TOON-Based Approach
detail.abstract: Financial document analysis increasingly relies on automated systems to process complex, multimodal information from quarterly (10-Q) and annual (10-K) reports. However, current retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems face a critical bottleneck: inefficient token consumption when encoding structured financial tables in formats like JSON. This study proposes and evaluates a TOON-based (Token-Optimized Object Notation) representation scheme for financial tables within a multimodal RAG framework. Three years (2023-2025) of Apple Inc. 10-K filings were extracted from SEC EDGAR API. A total of 90 large financial tables were extracted and compared token efficiency between JSON and TOON encodings using the cl100k_base tokenizer. Results indicate that TOON achieves an average token reduction of 47.65% and byte reduction of 36.14% relative to JSON. Distribution analysis confirms consistent savings with a median reduction of 48.81%. Correlation analysis shows moderate positive association between token reduction and table width (r = 0.4465) and total cell count (r = 0.3929), while higher numerical precision negatively impacts compression (r =-0.5149). Context window simulations under 4k, 8k, and 16k token budgets demonstrate that TOON approximately doubles effective evidence capacity. These findings suggest that TOON-based encoding can substantially improve evidence capacity in financial RAG systems, potentially enhancing numerical reasoning and multi-document synthesis capabilities while maintaining interpretability.

title: The Impact of Public Data on AI Innovation: Open Government Data Initiatives Encourage Local Healthcare AI Investment

detail.title: The Impact of Public Data on AI Innovation: Open Government Data Initiatives Encourage Local Healthcare AI Investment
detail.abstract: Public data infrastructure is often built to enhance transparency and accountability. Yet it is costly, its economic and innovation spillovers remain uncertain, and governments have responded with divergent data-opening strategies. We examine whether and how the launch of open government data portals (OGDPs) affects healthcare AI innovation, which spans upstream vendor development and downstream hospital investment. Healthcare is an apt setting: it is data-intensive, faces substantial regulatory uncertainty, and depends on both data availability and institutional support for AI deployment. Using a panel dataset of Chinese cities and a staggered difference-indifferences design, we measure downstream investment through hospitals' procurement of diagnostic and operational AI systems. We find that OGDP launches generate sustained increases in such investment, a result that holds across heterogeneity-robust estimators, matching, synthetic control, and alternative-explanation tests. Mechanism analyses point to two channels: data provision is a necessary baseline input, but governmental signaling emerges as the more proximate driver, as OGDPs convey credible policy commitment that reduces regulatory uncertainty and accelerates the translation of upstream AI development into downstream investment. The effect is further amplified where governments prioritize digitalization, healthcare demand is acute, and local AI vendors are abundant. Our findings position OGDPs as both digital infrastructure and institutional signals. We contribute to research on public data and AI innovation by distinguishing material from cognitive channels, to work on healthcare AI ecosystems by elevating the institutional layer, and to the literature on directed technical change, while offering guidance on realizing the broader impacts of public data.

detail.abstract: The artificial-intelligence industry has built an elaborate apparatus for ranking the factuality of what its language models say. Hallucination and faithfulness leaderboards now compare dozens of systems on how often an output is correct, or how faithfully it tracks a supplied source. This essay argues that the apparatus measures a symptom and leaves the disease unexamined. The question a reader most needs answered — whether the knowledge behind an output is epistemically grounded in validated fact or merely inherited from the unvalidated centroid of a web-scale corpus — is one that no current ranking addresses, and, under present practice, none can. The reason resolves into three nested quantities. The share of a frontier corpus certified token-by-token as factually true is, publicly, zero; the high-provenance reference material in the only disclosed mixes runs to the low single digits or mid-teens of a percent; and the fraction receiving any human factual scrutiny is a sliver, most of it not truth-verification at all. What can be ranked is not systems but data: the curated streams that steer a model vary in their proximity to a demonstrable truth-condition, and that ranking — benchmark and grounding data at the top, preference and prompt data at the bottom — maps onto the only region a curated corpus can certify, the formal and the atomic-empirical. Even there the ground is imperfect: the most-cited knowledge benchmark carries an estimated error rate above six percent. The honest constructive response is a provenance-and-warrant ledger, not a truth oracle, bounded to that certifiable core, with the synthesis residue returned to the human conductor. The argument is offered in the Popperian spirit, with the condition that would refute it stated plainly: a laboratory disclosing its corpus composition together with a per-source record of validation status.

title: The Worker Protection Act: Prevention or Illusion?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Worker Protection Act: Prevention or Illusion?
detail.abstract:
This report critically assesses the Worker Protection Act 2023 (the Act) and the updated technical guidance issued by the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC). While the Act introduces a preventative duty on employers to take reasonable steps to stop sexual harassment before it occurs, the practical effect of this shift remains limited. The duty cannot be enforced directly by employees unless a harassment claim is successful, meaning the system continues to operate reactively.

Several gaps reduce the Act’s effectiveness. It applies only to sexual harassment, excluding other protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010. It also fails to restore liability for third- party harassment, leaving many front-line workers without adequate protection. The absence of a statutory definition of “reasonable steps” contributes further to legal uncertainty, making it difficult for employers to assess their obligations.

The EHRC’s guidance provides helpful interpretation, but it is not legally binding, and enforcement depends on limited institutional capacity. Without clearer statutory benchmarks and stronger mechanisms, the Act risks falling short of its preventative aims.

Nevertheless, employers must still aim to comply. Tribunals are expected to rely on the EHRC guidance when assessing whether reasonable steps were taken and whether a compensation uplift should be awarded. Yet to reach that stage, a harassment claim must first succeed, a reality that keeps the duty tethered to a post-incident model rather than allowing for early intervention.

The June 2026 initial public offering of SpaceX at a valuation of $1.77 trillion, the largest IPO in recorded financial history marks a civilisational inflection point in the commercialisation of outer space. The event crystallises a structural transformation that has been underway since the early 2000s: the migration of space activity from state-monopolised strategic programmes toward commercially driven, venture-backed, defence-integrated ecosystems.

This paper uses the SpaceX IPO as an analytical catalyst to examine whether India can construct a globally competitive commercial space economy by 2047. Drawing on the Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe regulatory frameworks, Economic Survey 2025-26, Union Budget allocations through FY2026-27, global market intelligence reports, and the institutional literature on patient capital and industrial policy, this paper argues that India's NewSpace ambitions are credible but currently constrained by four structural gaps: the absence of assured government procurement pipelines, insufficient scale capital, regulatory ambiguities in the non-governmental entity (NGE) authorisation framework, and fragmented defence-space integration. title: Reversal of Great Gatsby: Is Educational Great Gatsby Curve U-shaped in Developing Countries?

detail.title: Reversal of Great Gatsby: Is Educational Great Gatsby Curve U-shaped in Developing Countries?
detail.abstract: We study educational Great Gatsby Curve (GGC) that posits a negative association between parental education inequality and children's relative educational mobility, with a focus on possible reversal beyond a threshold level of inequality (a U-shaped GGC). Our analysis addresses major methodological concerns: mechanical association between inequality and relative mobility, coresidency bias in measures of mobility, (non)comparability of data across sources, and robustness to alternative measures of inequality. We use sibling correlation (SC) and intergenerational correlation (IGC) as measures of relative mobility because they do not capture mechanical associations and are robust to coresidency bias. Gini coefficient and Atkinson index are used as measures of inequality. Our empirical analysis utilizes both crosscountry (66 developing countries) and sub-national panel data (2694 districts and four 5-year birth cohorts in 25 Sub Saharan African countries). The crosscountry data come from 277 waves of Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS), and the sub-national data from 10% samples of censuses in IPUMS International. We report three major findings. First, the linear specification yields misleading conclusions, suggesting no robust evidence of a educational GGC. Second, linearity is rejected (1% level) across the board irrespective of data sets and measures of mobility and inequality in favor of a convex GGC. In sub-national IPUMS panel, district and cohort fixed effects strengthen the convexity: the squared-Gini coefficient on sibling correlation is-2.064 (s.e. 0.219) with fixed effects versus-0.267 (s.e. 0.089) without. Third, the Lind and Mehlum (2010) U-test rejects monotonicity in favor of a U-shaped GGC in most specifications. In IPUMS panel with fixed effects, 49-51 percent of districts fall in the "wrong" part of the U-curve beyond the minimum point. The standard educational GGC therefore reverses at the upper tail of inequality for roughly half the districts in our SSA panel. In the 66-country DHS data, the share of countries in the inverse-GGC segment of the U-curve rises across cohorts, from about 29-41 percent in the 1970s to 45-54 percent in the 1990s.

title: Spatial Spillover Effects of Local Government Implicit Debt

detail.title: Spatial Spillover Effects of Local Government Implicit Debt
detail.abstract: In recent years, implicit debt of Chinese local governments has continued to accumulate. The 15th Five-Year Plan explicitly identifies the prevention and resolution of local government debt risks as a core task of fiscal security. Against the backdrop of highly interconnected regional economies, localized debt risks can readily spread across provinces through financial markets and government behavior channels, evolving into systemic threats. This paper uses the credit spread of municipal bond issued by local government financing vehicles (LGFVs) as a proxy for implicit debt risk. Based on daily data from 29 provincial administrative regions over 2015–2024, we introduce the Quantile Vector Autoregression (QVAR) model and network topology methods to systematically characterize the spatial spillover patterns and transmission pathways of interprovincial debt risk under different market states. We find that: interprovincial debt risk co-movement exhibits a significant U-shaped asymmetric structure, with co-movement under spread-widening stress states and spread-compression boom states both stronger than under normal conditions; net receivers are highly stable, with fiscally weak provinces such as Inner Mongolia, Gansu, and Qinghai consistently under pressure regardless of market state;while net transmitters undergo structural reorganization across different states, with the reverse contagion effect of weaker provinces emerging under spread-widening stress scenarios. Major shock events (COVID-19 pandemic, Evergrande default) can rapidly reshape the risk spillover network in the short term, with fiscally weak provinces quickly transitioning from a relatively independent state to become core nodes of systemic transmission. These findings provide empirical evidence for differentiated regional policy responses and the establishment of a cross-provincial coordinated prevention and control system.

title: Gender Disparities in Promotions: Evidence from Accounting Academia

detail.title: Gender Disparities in Promotions: Evidence from Accounting Academia
detail.abstract: Promotion decisions in academia are widely debated, including within accounting research. Yet, for our field as well as other major business disciplines, there is little systematic evidence on how long it takes researchers to be promoted, what determines time-to-promotion, and whether structural gender differences exist. This paper leverages résumé data of a large sample of accounting researchers (N = 1,357) to analyze variation in the likelihood and time required to attain the ranks of associate and full professor. We find that after controlling for key promotion determinants, female researchers face a lower likelihood to be promoted and take about 4.2% and 14.3% longer than male researchers to be promoted to associate and full professor (equivalent to 0.3 and 1.81 years), respectively. Cross-sectional tests reveal that these gender gaps are concentrated in researchers with relatively fewer top publications, degrees from lower-ranked PhD programs, or appointments at lower-ranked institutions or those without recognized DEI performance.

title: Who Profits in Binary Prediction Markets? Maker-Taker Dynamics, Behavioral Bias, and Sentiment Arbitrage on Kalshi

detail.title: Who Profits in Binary Prediction Markets? Maker-Taker Dynamics, Behavioral Bias, and Sentiment Arbitrage on Kalshi
detail.abstract: Whether liquidity providers in binary prediction markets systematically profit from uninformed order flow, and whether behavioral biases sustain that profit, remain open empirical questions. We address them using 72.1 million executed trades ($18.3B notional) on Kalshi from July 2021 through November 2025, supplemented by 404.5 million on-chain trades from Polymarket, applying volume-weighted return decomposition, calibration analysis, OLS regression, and paired t-tests. A statistically significant Favorite-Longshot Bias (FLSB) emerges on both platforms, but with a cross-platform contrast: Kalshi longshots are overpriced (δ b < 0, p < 0.001 for all sub-25% buckets) while Polymarket favorites above 55% implied probability are systematically underpriced (δ b > 0, t up to 361), implicating market design as the key moderating factor. On the supply side, makers earn +0.83 percentage points (pp) in volumeweighted returns (p = 0.0055), constituting a $142.5M wealth transfer that exceeds estimated bid-ask spread compensation by 0.13 pp. This alpha is not uniform: it ranges from +0.29 pp in Finance to +3.01 pp in World Events, with high-volume categories spanning +0.82 pp (Sports) to +1.78 pp (Media), consistent with adverse selection varying by information environment. On the demand side, takers allocate 63.8% of capital to YES contracts despite earning 0.32 pp less than NO-side takers, an affirmative framing bias unexplained by differential risk. Contrary to efficiency-convergence predictions, maker alpha trends upward at +8.21 bp/month (R 2 = 0.70) as retail participation grows. A sport-level decomposition of the dominant sports category (74% of volume) reveals maker alpha ranging from +0.18 pp in MLB to +3.43 pp in UFC/Boxing, with no significant time-to-resolution decay (p = 0.88), providing direct evidence of persistent fandriven sentiment arbitrage. Taken together, these findings indicate that binary prediction markets structurally disadvantage uninformed retail participants and call for targeted disclosure requirements and calibration-oriented regulatory oversight.

title: The Impact of COVID-19 on NJ Higher Education Institutions Enrollment, Retention, and Headcount: A Regional Panel Data Analysis

detail.title: The Impact of COVID-19 on NJ Higher Education Institutions Enrollment, Retention, and Headcount: A Regional Panel Data Analysis
detail.abstract: In 2020, COVID-19 disrupted the learning experiences of millions of students across the United States. Previous studies examining the shock impact of Covid-19 have not dealt with exploring the effects of state policy on the enrollment and retention of students in New Jersey. The methodology for this study uses the before-and-after effects model on 148 New Jersey institutions; the results were that the incoming enrollment went down by -212.87 students (p < 0.0001), a 6.7% decrease from the pre-covid era. However, we observed that the retention rate decreased -1.28% but didn’t show anything statistically significant  (p = 0.1498). Further empirical analysis found  that community colleges in NJ suffered more than non-community college institutions. The finding of this study suggests that New Jersey policies could not cushion the impact of Covid-19 for the students attending institutions of higher education. As a result, community colleges suffered.

title: When, Not Which Way: Move-Occurrence Predictability, Directional Efficiency, and Regime-Adaptive Clustering in Foreign-Exchange Tick Data
affiliations: Larkin Research Limited and Larkin Research Limited

detail.title: When, Not Which Way: Move-Occurrence Predictability, Directional Efficiency, and Regime-Adaptive Clustering in Foreign-Exchange Tick Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Both authors are principals of Larkin Research Limited. The research was internally funded; the authors declare no other competing interests. The paper makes no recommendation regarding any financial instrument.
declarations.funderStatement: The analysis pipeline, simulations and drafting were carried out with the assistance of an AI research assistant (Claude, Anthropic), under the direction and review of the authors, who take full responsibility for the methodology, results and conclusions.

detail.abstract: We study short-horizon price dynamics in foreign-exchange tick data, asking three nested questions: can the occurrence of an imminent price move be predicted; can its direction be predicted; and can either be monetised in spot trading? Using Dukascopy EUR/USD quotes (June 2022 training month; July–December 2022 and the whole of 2023 held out), we define a move as a first-passage excursion of at least 5 pips within 120 seconds and characterise each decision point by its trailing 600-second window. We report four findings. First, move occurrence is strongly predictable from trailing realised volatility: a four-feature logistic model trained on a single month attains a pooled out-of-sample AUC of 0.846 (95% day-block bootstrap CI [0.840, 0.852]) over 374,934 grid decision points spanning eighteen months, with the most confident 1% of points followed by a move 79.8% of the time against a 9.7% base rate (8.2× lift). The signal survives a time-of-day confound test (within-hour AUC 0.72–0.76) and is invariant to quote side. Second, direction is not predictable at decision time: a seventeen-feature battery including order-flow imbalance and micro-price predictors attains at most 0.53 AUC. We document a subtle and instructive artefact whereby the identical battery evaluated at retrospectively defined move-start ticks attains a spurious 0.82 AUC, traceable to the first-passage selection of the anchor itself. Third, the occurrence signal is not monetisable with direction-agnostic spot structures: tick-accurate breakout-straddle simulations lose approximately 0.35 pips per trade across all configurations, with post-trigger win rates statistically indistinguishable from the driftless-random-walk benchmark and quoted spreads widening by ~36% precisely in the gated windows. Fourth, the volatility regime itself drifts, and online mixture-model clustering with exponential forgetting tracks it — but the benefit is proportional to the non-stationary (volatility) content of the representation, a gradient we replicate on GBP/USD across the 2022 gilt-crisis-to-calm transition. We argue the joint pattern — predictable timing, unpredictable direction, defended spreads — is exactly what an efficient dealer market should produce, and that the methodological by-products (anchor-conditioning artefacts, base-rate transfer failure, prequential drift diagnostics) are of independent practical value.

title: Large Company Loses Billions of Dollars, Pays No Income Tax! Understanding the Ongoing Scandal
affiliations: University of Connecticut - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Large Company Loses Billions of Dollars, Pays No Income Tax! Understanding the Ongoing Scandal
detail.abstract: Every few years, headlines pop up claiming that "Insert Large Company Name" paid no income tax on massive amounts of income in one year or over a few years. These claims tend to be misguided or misleading for two primary reasons, which I explain in this note. First, the claims incorrectly assume that the tax system operates solely on an annual basis. Second, the claims fail to acknowledge that income is computed differently for tax purposes than for financial accounting, which uses Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).

title: Beyond Interest Income: Revenue Diversification and Financial Stability in Emerging Markets
affiliations: , Olin Business School, Washington University in St. Louis - Washington University in and American University

detail.title: Beyond Interest Income: Revenue Diversification and Financial Stability in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between non-interest income and bank earnings stability in emerging market banking systems, using panel evidence from 26 commercial banks over a six-year period. As financial sectors in developing economies increasingly diversify revenue sources beyond traditional intermediation, the stability implications of such diversification remain empirically contested. Guided by Modern Portfolio Theory, this study evaluates the effect of disaggregated components of non-interest income fees and commissions income, foreign exchange trading income, dividend income, and other operating income on bank insolvency risk measured by the Zscore. Quantitative research design was employed using balanced panel data, and both pooled Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and fixed effects regression models were estimated to account for time and bank-specific heterogeneity. The findings indicate that fees and commissions income and other operating income are positively associated with financial stability, suggesting that certain forms of revenue diversification enhance earnings resilience. In contrast, foreign exchange trading income and dividend income exhibit statistically insignificant effects on insolvency risk. The results demonstrate that the composition of non-interest income, rather than diversification per se, determines stability outcomes in emerging markets. These findings provide important implications for bank management and regulatory policy, highlighting the need for targeted diversification strategies that strengthen, rather than undermine, financial stability. Peer-reviewed version published in World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, Vol. 29(03), 2026.

title: Leadership, Mental Health, and Physical Work Environments: A Mixed-Methods Study of Employee Performance in Bali’s MICE Industry
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Griffith University

detail.title: Leadership, Mental Health, and Physical Work Environments: A Mixed-Methods Study of Employee Performance in Bali’s MICE Industry
detail.abstract: Employee mental health is a growing concern in high-demand service sectors, yet its relationship with job satisfaction and performance remains contested. In hospitality and events research, the happy–productive worker thesis assumes that satisfied employees are healthier and more productive; however, recent studies suggest this link depends on contextual resources, leadership, and ergonomics. In Bali’s Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (MICE) industry, post-pandemic recovery, irregular hours, and demanding clients intensify psychological strain, while culturally embedded leadership and diverse work environments complicate existing models.This study integrates Job Demands–Resources theory, Self-Determination Theory, and eudaimonic well-being to examine how leadership style, physical work environment, mental health, and job satisfaction shape employee performance. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design combines survey data from 146 professionals with semi-structured interviews with 18 practitioners in Bali’s MICE and luxury wedding sectors. The structural model tests five hypotheses, while qualitative analysis explores competence mastery and ergonomics as well-being resources.Findings show that supportive and transformational leadership strongly predicts satisfaction and performance. Job satisfaction does not significantly explain mental health, which is more closely linked to performance and physical conditions. These results challenge the generalizability of the happy–productive worker thesis in high-pressure contexts and highlight competence and ergonomics as key eudaimonic resources. The study refines JD–R and SDT in a tourism-specific setting and offers practical insights for leadership development and workplace design to support a sustainable, mentally healthy MICE workforce in Bali.
